photoobj_row_level.name: photoobj_row_level
photoobj_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.mjd,
  p.loadversion
FROM
  photoobj p
photoobj_row_level.description: Canonical row-level photographic detections with primary identification, positional and photometric columns normalized for downstream filtering and joins.

photo_type_lookup.name: photo_type_lookup
photo_type_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value AS value,
  pt.name AS name,
  pt.description AS description
FROM
  photo_type pt
ORDER BY
  pt.value
photo_type_lookup.description: Lookup table mapping photo_type.value to its name and description for filtering/classification of photoobj.type.
validated_on: Find the object ids, right ascensions and declinations of photometrically observable galaxy whose right ascension is greater than 185, right ascension is less than 186, declination is greater than 15, declination is less than 16.
Show me object id, right ascensions and declinations of photometrically observed galaxy in a certain area, of which the right ascension is between 185 and 186, declination is bertween 15 and 16.

Find the object ids, right ascensions and declinations of photometrically observable star whose right ascension is greater than 185, right ascension is less than 186, declination is greater than 15, declination is less than 16.
Find the number of photometrically observed GALAXY whose magnitude r is less than 17, extinction r is greater than 0.2.

Find all photometric observable GALAXY whose magnitude g is brighter than 22, the difference of magnitude u and magnitude g is between -0.27 and 0.71, the difference of magnitude g and magnitude r is between -0.24 and 0.35, the difference of magnitude r and magnitude i is between -0.27 and 0.57 and the difference of magnitude i and magnitude z is between -0.35 and 0.7. Retrieve the object id and magnitude g with descent order by magnitude g.
counter_examples: Show me all photometrically observable star
How many photometrically observable GALAXY of which magnitude r is lower than 17 and extinction r is higher than 0.2.

photoobj_with_type_name.name: photoobj_with_type_name
photoobj_with_type_name.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.type AS type,
  t.name AS type_name,
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,
  p.r AS r,
  p.i AS i,
  p.z AS z,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.run AS run,
  p.field AS field,
  p.rerun AS rerun,
  p.clean AS clean
FROM photoobj_row_level p
LEFT JOIN photo_type_lookup t
  ON p.type = t.value
photoobj_with_type_name.description: Denormalized photoobj rows augmented with the photo_type.name to allow easy classification-based cohorts (e.g., STAR).

photoobj_base_rows.name: photoobj_base_rows
photoobj_base_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  po.objid::bigint AS objid,
  po.ra::double precision AS ra,
  po.dec::double precision AS dec,
  po.u::real AS u,
  po.g::real AS g,
  po.r::real AS r,
  po.i::real AS i,
  po.z::real AS z,
  po.type::integer AS type,
  po.clean::integer AS clean,
  po.flags::bigint AS flags
FROM photoobj AS po
photoobj_base_rows.description: Canonical, cleaned projection of the photoobj table exposing primary id, positions, photometry, type and basic quality flags. Nulls are preserved so downstream filters can choose (e.g., require at least one magnitude).
validated_on: Show me object id, right ascensions and declinations of photometrically observed galaxy in a certain area, of which the right ascension is between 185 and 186, declination is bertween 15 and 16.

Fetch me the object id, right ascension, declination, and redshift of spectroscopic observed star in a certain area, of which the right ascension is in an unbouded interval of 185 and 186, declination is in an unbouded interval of 15 and 16.

Show me the object id, right ascension and declination of photometrically observed Galaxy, of which the the right ascension in a range of from 140.9 to 141.1, the magnitude g is less than 18.0 and the difference of magnitude u and g is higher than 2.2

photoobj_base.name: photoobj_base
photoobj_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  p.run::smallint AS run,
  p.field::smallint AS field,
  p.rowc::real AS rowc,
  p.colc::real AS colc,
  p.u::real AS u,
  p.g::real AS g,
  p.r::real AS r,
  p.i::real AS i,
  p.z::real AS z,
  p.type::integer AS type,
  p.clean::integer AS clean,
  p.flags::bigint AS flags
FROM photoobj p
WHERE p.objid IS NOT NULL
  -- liftable literals for downstream filters: keep only canonical detections with non-null position
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
photoobj_base.description: Canonical photo objects with core positional and identifier columns normalized for downstream joins and filters.
counter_examples: Find all photometrically observable Galaxy that have spectral observations. Retrieve the object id, right ascension, and declination.

specobj_base.name: specobj_base
specobj_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  specobj.specobjid::numeric                          AS specobjid,
  specobj.bestobjid::bigint                            AS bestobjid,
  specobj.plate::smallint                              AS plate,
  specobj.mjd::integer                                 AS mjd,
  specobj.fiberid::smallint                            AS fiberid,
  specobj.ra::double precision                         AS ra,
  specobj.dec::double precision                        AS dec,
  specobj.z::real                                      AS z,
  specobj.class::character varying                     AS class
FROM
  specobj
specobj_base.description: Canonical spectral observation records exposing the linking key to photometry (bestobjid) and core spectral metadata.
counter_examples: Show me the object id, right ascension, and declination of photometrically observed star that have spectral observations.

photoobj_with_best_spec.name: photoobj_with_best_spec
photoobj_with_best_spec.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid                                          AS objid,
  p.ra                                             AS photo_ra,
  p.dec                                            AS photo_dec,
  s.specobjid                                      AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid                                      AS spec_bestobjid,
  s.ra                                             AS spec_ra,
  s.dec                                            AS spec_dec,
  s.z                                              AS z,
  s.class                                          AS class
FROM photoobj_base p
JOIN specobj_base s
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
photoobj_with_best_spec.description: Photo objects that have at least one linked spectrum where specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid (denormalized relation for objects present in both catalogs). One row per photo object per matching specobj.

photoobj_core.name: photoobj_core
photoobj_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS object_id,
  p.ra     AS right_ascension,
  p.dec    AS declination
FROM
  photoobj_base p
photoobj_core.description: Canonical projection of photometric objects with core identifying columns, positional coordinates, photometric type code and basic photometry. Nulls left as-is; no question-specific filtering.

photo_with_spectrum_link.name: photo_with_spectrum_link
photo_with_spectrum_link.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  p.objid AS object_id,
  p.ra    AS right_ascension,
  p.dec   AS declination
FROM photoobj p
JOIN specobj s
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
photo_with_spectrum_link.description: Denormalized join that yields photoobj rows that have at least one matching spectrum via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid. One row per photometric object; duplicates eliminated by DISTINCT on photoobj.objid.

photoobj_base_9.name: photoobj_base_9
photoobj_base_9.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,

  p.z,

  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.extinction_r
FROM photoobj p
photoobj_base_9.description: Canonical normalized photo object rows with primary identifying and photometric columns. Casts/cleans are kept minimal (no filtering) so this view can serve as a base for cohorts and joins.
validated_on: Find the object ids, right ascensions and declinations of photometrically observable star whose right ascension is greater than 185, right ascension is less than 186, declination is greater than 15, declination is less than 16.
counter_examples: Show me the object id, right ascension, declination, and redshift of spectroscopic observed galaxy in a certain area, of which the right ascension is in an unbouded interval of 185 and 186, declination is in an unbouded interval of 15 and 16.

Find all photometrically observable star with a difference of magnitude u and magnitude g is less than 0.4,  the difference between magnitude g and magnitude r is less than 0.7, the difference between magnitude r and magnitude i is greater than 0.4 and the difference between magnitude i and magnitude z is greater than 0.4

Find object id, right ascension, declination of photometrically observed star whose magnitude i is brighter than 19 and fainter than 0, the difference of magnitude g and magnitude r is higher than 2.26, the difference of magnitude i and magnitude z is lower than 0.25, and either the difference of magnitude u and magnitude g is greater than 2.0 or magnitude u is fainter than 22.3

photo_type_lookup_10.name: photo_type_lookup_10
photo_type_lookup_10.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.value::integer AS value,
  p.name AS name,
  p.description AS description
FROM photo_type p
photo_type_lookup_10.description: Lookup table for photo type codes to their names and descriptions. Use to translate photoobj.type codes into stable textual categories (e.g. 'GALAXY').
validated_on: Show me object id, right ascensions and declinations of photometrically observed star in a certain area, of which the right ascension is between 185 and 186, declination is bertween 15 and 16.
counter_examples: Find all spectroscopic observed star,  whose right ascension is greater than 185 and less than 186, declination is greater than 15 and less than 16. Retrieve their object id, right ascension, declination, and photometric object type

Find object id, right ascension, declination of photometrically observed star whose magnitude i is brighter than 19 and fainter than 0, the difference of magnitude g and magnitude r is higher than 2.26, the difference of magnitude i and magnitude z is lower than 0.25, and either the difference of magnitude u and magnitude g is greater than 2.0 or magnitude u is fainter than 22.3

photoobj_with_type.name: photoobj_with_type
photoobj_with_type.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  pt.name AS type_name,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.extinction_r
FROM photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type.description: Denormalized photo objects joined to photo_type names so queries can filter/label objects by their type name in a single relation.
validated_on: What are the photometrically observable Galaxy whose right ascension is between 140.9 and 141.1, magnitude g is brighter than 18.0 and the difference of magitude u and magnitude g is greater than 2.2. Retrieve the objecti id, right ascension and declination of these objects.

specobj_galaxy_cohort.name: specobj_galaxy_cohort
specobj_galaxy_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.class,
  s.ra,
  s.dec,
  s.z,
  s.mjd
FROM specobj s
WHERE s.class = 'GALAXY'
  AND s.bestobjid IS NOT NULL
  -- Ensure linked photometric object exists in photoobj (lift photometric table literal)
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM photoobj p WHERE p.objid = s.bestobjid
  )
specobj_galaxy_cohort.description: Cohort of spectroscopic objects that are classified as galaxies and have a linked photometric object (bestobjid present). Exposes spectroscopic id, matched photometric id, spectroscopic class and key spectroscopic columns useful for joins/filters.

photoobj_photometry.name: photoobj_photometry
photoobj_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  p.u::real AS u,
  p.g::real AS g,
  p.r::real AS r,
  p.i::real AS i,
  p.z::real AS z,
  p.clean::integer AS clean,
  p.run::smallint AS run,
  p.field::smallint AS field,
  p.type::smallint AS type
FROM photoobj_base p
WHERE p.clean IS NOT NULL
photoobj_photometry.description: Canonicalized photometric detections with positional and photometric columns. Normalizes/filters to rows where the 'clean' flag exists (not null) and exposes magnitudes; useful as the photometric side for joins to spectroscopy.

specphoto_joined.name: specphoto_joined
specphoto_joined.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid                                  AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid                                   AS bestobjid,
  s.class                                       AS class,
  s.ra                                          AS spec_ra,
  s.dec                                         AS spec_dec,
  p.objid                                       AS objid,
  p.ra                                          AS photo_ra,
  p.dec                                         AS photo_dec,
  p.u                                           AS u,
  p.g                                           AS g,
  p.r                                           AS r,
  p.i                                           AS i,
  p.z                                           AS z,
  p.clean                                       AS clean
FROM specobj AS s
JOIN photoobj AS p
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
WHERE s.bestobjid IS NOT NULL
  AND p.clean IS NOT NULL
specphoto_joined.description: Denormalized join of spectroscopic objects to their matched photometric detections. Produces one row per specobj.specobjid joined to photoobj via bestobjid=objid. Filters are minimal (specobj.bestobjid IS NOT NULL and photoobj.clean IS NOT NULL) to remain generally useful.

spectroscopic_objects_core.name: spectroscopic_objects_core
spectroscopic_objects_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  s.class::text AS class,
  s.subclass::text AS subclass,
  s.z::real AS z,
  s.mjd::integer AS mjd,
  s.plate::smallint AS plate,
  s.fiberid::smallint AS fiberid
FROM specobj AS s
spectroscopic_objects_core.description: Canonical projection of spectroscopic objects (specobj) exposing links to photometric objects (bestobjid) and primary identifiers; one row per specobj.

photo_with_spectra_link.name: photo_with_spectra_link
photo_with_spectra_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.type AS type,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid AS bestobjid,
  s.z AS z
FROM photoobj p
JOIN specobj s
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
photo_with_spectra_link.description: Denormalized join that associates photoobj rows to any matching specobj rows via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid. One row per photoobj/specobj pair. Useful to select photometric objects that have at least one spectrum and to access spectral attributes next to photometric ones.

photoobj_basic_positions.name: photoobj_basic_positions
photoobj_basic_positions.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary identifier from photoobj
  p.objid AS objid,

  -- canonical sky coordinates: prefer non-null ra/dec from photoobj;
  -- normalize NULLs to NULL (explicit) — no transformation needed, but
  -- keep numeric types consistent by casting to double precision.
  (CASE WHEN p.ra IS NOT NULL THEN p.ra::double precision ELSE NULL END) AS ra,
  (CASE WHEN p.dec IS NOT NULL THEN p.dec::double precision ELSE NULL END) AS dec

FROM photoobj AS p
photoobj_basic_positions.description: Canonical projection of photometric objects with their primary identifiers and sky coordinates, exposing basic quality and coordinate columns and normalizing NULLs.

specobj_classification.name: specobj_classification
specobj_classification.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.class,
  s.subclass
FROM specobj s
specobj_classification.description: Projection of spectroscopic records with their object linkage and classification fields, exposing specobj primary id, the best matched photo object id, and spectral class/subclass.

photo_with_spectrum_join.name: photo_with_spectrum_join
photo_with_spectrum_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.class AS spec_class
FROM photoobj p
JOIN specobj s
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
photo_with_spectrum_join.description: Join of photometric objects to their matching spectroscopic records via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid, producing one row per photoobj - specobj match so queries can filter by spectral class while keeping photo coordinates.

photoobj_galaxy_cohort.name: photoobj_galaxy_cohort
photoobj_galaxy_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.type,
  pt.name AS photo_type_name
FROM
  photoobj p
JOIN
  photo_type pt
    ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE
  pt.name LIKE 'GAL%'
  OR pt.name = 'GALAXY'
  OR pt.name = 'galaxy'
  OR pt.name ILIKE '%galaxy%'

semantic_filters.photo_type.name: GALAXY (string match; exact name depends on catalog entries)

photoobj_galaxy_cohort.description: Cohort of photometrically observed objects that are galaxies (one row per photoobj.objid). This view combines photoobj with the photo_type lookup to expose only rows whose photo_type.name indicates a galaxy; keeps canonical columns for coordinate and id-level filtering.

photoobj_galaxy_cohort_21.name: photoobj_galaxy_cohort_21
photoobj_galaxy_cohort_21.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid                                          AS objid,
  p.ra                                             AS ra,
  p.dec                                            AS dec,
  p.type                                           AS type,
  pt.name                                          AS name,
  p.u                                              AS u,
  p.g                                              AS g,
  p.r                                              AS r,
  p.i                                              AS i,
  p.z                                              AS z,
  p.clean                                          AS clean
FROM photoobj p
JOIN photo_type pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE pt.name = 'GALAXY'
photoobj_galaxy_cohort_21.description: Cohort of photoobj rows that correspond to objects classified as galaxies (denormalized join to photo_type); exposes full photoobj row plus photo_type.name for easy filtering by object class.

photoobj_star_cohort.name: photoobj_star_cohort
photoobj_star_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.type,
  pt.name AS photo_type_name
FROM photoobj_base p
JOIN photo_type pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE pt.name = 'star'
photoobj_star_cohort.description: Cohort of photometric objects that are stars (joined to photo_type) but without spatial bounds applied. Exposes object id and coordinates for downstream spatial filtering and aggregation.

photoobj_point_sources.name: photoobj_point_sources
photoobj_point_sources.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra    AS ra,
  p.dec   AS dec,
  p.type  AS type
FROM photoobj_base p
WHERE
  -- select only point-like sources by type code: lift literal for maintainability
  p.type = 6
  -- require a valid position
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
  -- optional: prefer clean detections (lift literal)
  AND p.clean = 1
photoobj_point_sources.description: All photometric detections (photoobj) as a reusable row-level cohort of sources with their positional and classification attributes.

photoobj_with_type_name_24.name: photoobj_with_type_name_24
photoobj_with_type_name_24.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.type,
  pt.name AS photo_type_name,
  pt.description AS photo_type_description
FROM
  photoobj p
LEFT JOIN
  photo_type pt
ON
  p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_name_24.description: Denormalized photoobj rows augmented with the photo type name/description so queries can filter by type name (e.g., 'star') without repeating joins.

spectroscopic_objects_core_25.name: spectroscopic_objects_core_25
spectroscopic_objects_core_25.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  s.ra::double precision AS ra,
  s.dec::double precision AS dec,
  s.class::character varying AS class,
  s.mjd::integer AS mjd,
  s.plate::smallint AS plate,
  s.fiberid::smallint AS fiberid
FROM
  specobj AS s
spectroscopic_objects_core_25.description: One-row-per-spectroscopic-observation with core spectroscopic columns and keys; useful as a cohort for filtering by class, ra/dec, mjd, plate/fiber, and linking to photometry via bestobjid.

photo_objects_basic.name: photo_objects_basic
photo_objects_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra    AS ra,
  p.dec   AS dec,
  p.u     AS u,
  p.g     AS g,
  p.r     AS r,
  p.i     AS i,
  p.z     AS z,
  p.type  AS type,
  p.run   AS run,
  p.field AS field,
  p.mode  AS mode,
  p.clean AS clean
FROM photoobj_row_level p
photo_objects_basic.description: One-row-per-photometric-object with positional, photometric magnitudes, type code, and object key for joins to spectroscopic tables.

specobj_basic_class_redshift.name: specobj_basic_class_redshift
specobj_basic_class_redshift.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  s.class::varchar AS class,
  s.z::real AS z,
  s.zerr::real AS zerr,
  s.mjd::integer AS mjd,
  s.plate::smallint AS plate,
  s.fiberid::smallint AS fiberid
FROM specobj s
specobj_basic_class_redshift.description: One row per spectroscopic object exposing its primary linked photometric object id (bestobjid), classification, redshift and spectrum metadata for filtering by class and joining to photo objects.

photoobj_with_specobj_link.name: photoobj_with_specobj_link
photoobj_with_specobj_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra    AS ra,
  p.dec   AS dec,
  s.bestobjid AS bestobjid,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.class     AS class,
  s.z         AS z
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN specobj s
  ON p.objid = s.bestobjid
photoobj_with_specobj_link.description: Denormalized row per photoobj joined to its spectroscopic primary (if any), exposing photo coordinates and the linked spec row's class and redshift to support spatial+spectral queries.

specobj_row.name: specobj_row
specobj_row.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid::numeric AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid::bigint AS bestobjid,
  s.plateid::numeric AS plateid,
  s.scienceprimary::smallint AS scienceprimary,
  s.segue2primary::smallint AS segue2primary,
  s.survey::character varying AS survey,
  s.programname::character varying AS programname,
  s.mjd::integer AS mjd,
  s.plate::smallint AS plate,
  s.fiberid::smallint AS fiberid,
  s.special_target1::bigint AS special_target1,
  s.segue2_target1::bigint AS segue2_target1,
  s.segue2_target2::bigint AS segue2_target2,
  s.ancillary_target1::bigint AS ancillary_target1,
  s.ra::double precision AS ra,
  s.dec::double precision AS dec,
  s.z::real AS z,
  s.zerr::real AS zerr,
  s.zwarning::integer AS zwarning,
  s.class::character varying AS class,
  s.subclass::character varying AS subclass,
  s.veldisp::real AS veldisp,
  s.veldisperr::real AS veldisperr,
  s.loadversion::integer AS loadversion
FROM specobj s
specobj_row.description: Normalized/spec-level rows exposing all specobj columns (one row per spectroscopic observation). Casts/cleanup can be applied here in future; no question-specific filters.
validated_on: Find the object id, right ascension and declination of spectroscopic Galaxy, which have value of magnitude g between 17 and 18 and redshift less than 0.05.

Fetch me the object id, right ascension and declination of spectroscopic Galaxy with the color band magnitude g brighter than 18.0 but fainter than 17 and redshift lower than 0.05

photoobj_row.body_sql:

  pb.rerun,
  pb.field,
  pb.mode,
  pb.type,
  pb.clean,
  pb.flags,
  pb.rowc,

  pb.l,

  pb.u,
  pb.g,
  pb.r,

FROM photoobj pb
photoobj_row.description: Normalized/photo-level rows exposing all photoobj columns (one row per photometric object).
validated_on: Find the number of photometrically observed GALAXY whose magnitude r is less than 17, extinction r is greater than 0.2.

What are the photometrically observable Galaxy whose right ascension is between 140.9 and 141.1, magnitude g is brighter than 18.0 and the difference of magitude u and magnitude g is greater than 2.2. Retrieve the objecti id, right ascension and declination of these objects.
Find the object id, right ascension and declination of spectroscopic Galaxy, which have value of magnitude g between 17 and 18 and redshift less than 0.05.
counter_examples: Find all star in photometrically observable binary star system, of which the neighbor's distance less than 0.05,  the difference of magnitude u and magnitude g is lower than 0.4, the difference of magnitude g and magnitude r is lower than 0.7, the difference of magnitude r and magnitude i is higher than 0.4 and the difference of magnitude i and magnitude z is higher than 0.4
How many photometrically observable GALAXY of which magnitude r is lower than 17 and extinction r is higher than 0.2.

Show me the photometrically observable star with the color band magnitude i brighter than 19 but fainter than 0, the difference of magnitude g and r is greater than 2.26, the difference of magnitude i and z is less than 0.25, and either the difference of magnitude u and g is greater than 2.0 or the color band magnitude u is fainter than 22.3
Fetch me the object id, right ascension and declination of spectroscopic Galaxy with the color band magnitude g brighter than 18.0 but fainter than 17 and redshift lower than 0.05

specobj_photoobj_join.name: specobj_photoobj_join
specobj_photoobj_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.specobjid,
  s.bestobjid,
  s.plateid,
  s.scienceprimary,
  s.segue2primary,
  s.survey,
  s.programname,
  s.mjd,
  s.plate,
  s.fiberid,
  s.special_target1,
  s.segue2_target1,
  s.segue2_target2,
  s.ancillary_target1,
  s.ra,
  s.dec,
  s.z,
  s.zerr,
  s.zwarning,
  s.class,
  s.subclass,
  s.veldisp,
  s.veldisperr,
  s.loadversion,
  p.objid AS photoobj_objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode    AS photoobj_mode,
  p.type    AS photoobj_type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.ra      AS photoobj_ra,
  p.dec     AS photoobj_dec,
  p.b,
  p.l,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.mjd     AS photoobj_mjd,
  p.loadversion AS photoobj_loadversion,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z      AS photoobj_z
FROM specobj s
LEFT JOIN photoobj p
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
specobj_photoobj_join.description: Denormalized join of specobj to its matched photoobj via specobj.bestobjid = photoobj.objid. One row per specobj (specobjid) with the matched photoobj columns; does not apply question-specific spatial filters or class filters.

photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid.name: photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid
photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,
  p.r AS r,
  p.i AS i,
  p.z AS z,
  s.z AS spec_z,
  s.zerr AS spec_zerr,
  s.zwarning AS spec_zwarning,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid
FROM photoobj AS p
LEFT JOIN specobj AS s
  ON s.bestobjid = p.objid
photoobj_join_specobj_by_bestobjid.description: Denormalized one-row-per-photometric-object joined to its matched spectroscopic record (when present) via specobj.bestobjid -> photoobj.objid. Exposes both photometric position/magnitudes and spectroscopic redshift and quality flags. Designed for spatial-spectroscopic cohorts.

photo_type_star_codes.name: photo_type_star_codes
photo_type_star_codes.body_sql:
SELECT
  pt.value,
  pt.name
FROM
  photo_type pt
WHERE
  lower(coalesce(pt.name, '')) LIKE '%' || 'star' || '%'
photo_type_star_codes.description: Set of photo_type.value codes whose name indicates 'star' (case-insensitive match). This maps human label 'star' to underlying integer codes used in photoobj.type.

photoobj_spatial_and_observation_index.name: photoobj_spatial_and_observation_index
photoobj_spatial_and_observation_index.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mjd,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.mode
FROM photoobj_row_level AS p

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic filters; provides full index of photo detections

photoobj_spatial_and_observation_index.description: A selectable/cohort view exposing positional and observation identifiers for photoobj rows to support spatial filtering, neighbor joins, and grouping by observing run/field.

neighbors_within_distance.name: neighbors_within_distance
neighbors_within_distance.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid AS objid,
  n.neighborobjid AS neighborobjid,
  n.distance AS distance,
  n.type AS type,
  n.neighbortype AS neighbortype,
  n.mode AS mode,
  n.neighbormode AS neighbormode
FROM
  neighbors n
neighbors_within_distance.description: Neighbors pairs at the neighbor-row grain, exposing object ids and separation distance and neighbor relationship types. One row per neighbors row (objid, neighborobjid, distance).

photoobj_neighbor_denorm.name: photoobj_neighbor_denorm
photoobj_neighbor_denorm.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance
FROM photoobj p
JOIN neighbors n
  ON p.objid = n.objid

semantic_filters.photoobj.u: may be NULL (do not filter here); final query should require non-NULL photometry

photoobj_neighbor_denorm.description: Denormalized join of photoobj rows to their neighbor rows: one row per neighbor relation with left side photo object photometry and neighbor id/distance. Useful for queries about close pairs and paired photometry filters.

photoobj_clean_photometry.name: photoobj_clean_photometry
photoobj_clean_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM
  photoobj_base p
WHERE
  -- keep only rows with non-null raw magnitudes (required for color calculations)
  p.u IS NOT NULL
  AND p.g IS NOT NULL
  AND p.r IS NOT NULL
  AND p.i IS NOT NULL
  AND p.z IS NOT NULL
  -- optionally prefer clean photometry (lifted literal; set to 1 to require clean=1, or NULL to skip)
  AND (p.clean = 1 OR p.clean IS NULL OR TRUE)
photoobj_clean_photometry.description: Canonical per-photometric-object row with primary photometry columns and positional info; filters out rows with NULL magnitudes and keeps raw magnitudes and coordinates for color calculations.

neighbors_close_pairs.name: neighbors_close_pairs
neighbors_close_pairs.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.objid,
  n.neighborobjid,
  n.distance,
  n.type,
  n.neighbortype,
  n.mode,
  n.neighbormode
FROM
  neighbors n
neighbors_close_pairs.description: Row-level neighbor relationships between objects. One row per neighbor link (neighbors.objid, neighbors.neighborobjid) including separation and neighbor types/modes so queries can filter by distance or neighbor properties.

photoobj_colors.name: photoobj_colors
photoobj_colors.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid::bigint AS objid,
  p.u::double precision AS u,
  p.g::double precision AS g,
  p.r::double precision AS r,
  p.i::double precision AS i,
  p.z::double precision AS z,
  -- color differences computed as (bluer - redder)
  (p.u - p.g)::double precision AS u_g,
  (p.g - p.r)::double precision AS g_r,
  (p.r - p.i)::double precision AS r_i,
  (p.i - p.z)::double precision AS i_z
FROM photoobj AS p
photoobj_colors.description: Per-photoobj computed color differences derived from canonical photometry: u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z. One row per photoobj with the raw magnitudes and computed color measures to simplify color cuts and further aggregation.

photoobj_galaxy_cohort_40.name: photoobj_galaxy_cohort_40
photoobj_galaxy_cohort_40.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.type,
  p.r,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.ra,
  p.dec
FROM photoobj AS p
JOIN photo_type AS pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE pt.name = 'GALAXY'
  AND p.objid IS NOT NULL
photoobj_galaxy_cohort_40.description: Cohort of photometric objects that are classified (by photo_type) as GALAXY; exposes per-object columns for counting and further filtering.

photoobj_basic_photometry.name: photoobj_basic_photometry
photoobj_basic_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  -- null-filter numeric magnitudes: keep as-is (they are numeric/real), but coerce impossible sentinel values to NULL if needed.
  -- Lifted literals: none required; simple pass-through with safe numeric casts.
  CASE WHEN p.u IS NOT NULL THEN p.u::double precision ELSE NULL END AS u,
  CASE WHEN p.g IS NOT NULL THEN p.g::double precision ELSE NULL END AS g,
  CASE WHEN p.r IS NOT NULL THEN p.r::double precision ELSE NULL END AS r,
  CASE WHEN p.i IS NOT NULL THEN p.i::double precision ELSE NULL END AS i,
  CASE WHEN p.z IS NOT NULL THEN p.z::double precision ELSE NULL END AS z,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  p.type
FROM photoobj_row_level p
WHERE p.objid IS NOT NULL
photoobj_basic_photometry.description: One-row-per-photometric-object canonicalized photometry and positional columns with null-filtered numeric magnitudes exposed for safe numeric comparisons.

photoobj_with_type_name_42.name: photoobj_with_type_name_42
photoobj_with_type_name_42.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.u::double precision AS u,
  p.g::double precision AS g,
  p.r::double precision AS r,
  p.i::double precision AS i,
  p.z::double precision AS z,
  p.ra::double precision AS ra,
  p.dec::double precision AS dec,
  p.type AS type,
  pt.name AS type_name
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN photo_type pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_name_42.description: Denormalized photometric objects joined to their type name; exposes photometry and textual type for predicate convenience.

photoobj_galaxy_photometry.name: photoobj_galaxy_photometry
photoobj_galaxy_photometry.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z
FROM photoobj_row_level p
JOIN photo_type_lookup t ON p.type = t.value
WHERE t.name = 'GALAXY'
photoobj_galaxy_photometry.description: One-row-per-photometric-object cohort restricted to objects classified as galaxies (joins photoobj to photo_type) and exposes raw ugriz photometry and positional identifiers for downstream color cuts and filtering.
validated_on: Show me the object id, right ascension and declination of photometrically observed Galaxy, of which the the right ascension in a range of from 140.9 to 141.1, the magnitude g is less than 18.0 and the difference of magnitude u and g is higher than 2.2

photoobj_color_differences.name: photoobj_color_differences
photoobj_color_differences.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.u     AS u,
  p.g     AS g,
  p.r     AS r,
  p.i     AS i,
  p.z     AS z,
  -- compute color differences only when both bands are non-null; otherwise NULL
  CASE WHEN p.u IS NOT NULL AND p.g IS NOT NULL THEN p.u - p.g ELSE NULL END AS u_minus_g,
  CASE WHEN p.g IS NOT NULL AND p.r IS NOT NULL THEN p.g - p.r ELSE NULL END AS g_minus_r,
  CASE WHEN p.r IS NOT NULL AND p.i IS NOT NULL THEN p.r - p.i ELSE NULL END AS r_minus_i,
  CASE WHEN p.i IS NOT NULL AND p.z IS NOT NULL THEN p.i - p.z ELSE NULL END AS i_minus_z
FROM photoobj p
photoobj_color_differences.description: Normalized projection that computes common color differences (u-g, g-r, r-i, i-z) alongside original photometry for each photometric object. Keeps one row per photoobj and does null-preserving computations (computes color only when both bands non-NULL).

photoobj_galaxy_photometry_with_colors.name: photoobj_galaxy_photometry_with_colors
photoobj_galaxy_photometry_with_colors.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  -- color differences lifted as expressions (no literals embedded)
  (p.u - p.g) AS u_minus_g,
  (p.g - p.r) AS g_minus_r,
  (p.r - p.i) AS r_minus_i,
  (p.i - p.z) AS i_minus_z
FROM
  photoobj p
WHERE
  -- keep one-row-per-objid grain: objid is primary key in photoobj
  p.objid IS NOT NULL
photoobj_galaxy_photometry_with_colors.description: Denormalized per-photoobj row combining galaxy classification (photo_type), raw photometry, positions, and precomputed color differences to support selection by magnitude and multi-color cuts.

photometry_star_candidates.name: photometry_star_candidates
photometry_star_candidates.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.u AS u,
  p.g AS g,
  p.r AS r,
  p.i AS i,
  p.z AS z,
  p.type AS type,
  pt.name AS type_name,
  -- computed colors (lift literals: none)
  (p.g - p.r) AS g_minus_r,
  (p.i - p.z) AS i_minus_z,
  (p.u - p.g) AS u_minus_g
FROM photoobj_row_level p
LEFT JOIN photo_type_lookup pt
  ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE p.objid IS NOT NULL
photometry_star_candidates.description: Row-level cohort of photoobj rows that are candidates for 'star' selections: denormalized join to photo_type to tag objects by type name. Keeps one row per photoobj and exposes magnitudes and computed colors for convenient filtering in downstream queries.

photoobj_color_indices.name: photoobj_color_indices
photoobj_color_indices.body_sql:
SELECT
  po.objid,
  po.u,
  po.g,
  po.r,
  po.i,
  po.z,
  po.cmodelmag_u,
  po.cmodelmag_g,
  po.cmodelmag_r,
  -- color indices: NULL when any input mag is NULL
  CASE WHEN po.g IS NOT NULL AND po.r IS NOT NULL THEN po.g - po.r ELSE NULL END AS g_minus_r,
  CASE WHEN po.i IS NOT NULL AND po.z IS NOT NULL THEN po.i - po.z ELSE NULL END AS i_minus_z,
  CASE WHEN po.u IS NOT NULL AND po.g IS NOT NULL THEN po.u - po.g ELSE NULL END AS u_minus_g,
  -- presence/validity flags: true when magnitude IS NOT NULL
  (po.u IS NOT NULL) AS has_u,
  (po.g IS NOT NULL) AS has_g,
  (po.r IS NOT NULL) AS has_r,
  (po.i IS NOT NULL) AS has_i,
  (po.z IS NOT NULL) AS has_z
FROM photoobj po
photoobj_color_indices.description: Per-photoobj computed color indices and basic validity flags (no aggregation across objid). Exposes commonly used color differences and flags indicating presence/absence of magnitudes to simplify filter expressions in downstream queries.

photoobj_galaxy_cohort_48.name: photoobj_galaxy_cohort_48
photoobj_galaxy_cohort_48.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.type
FROM photoobj_base p
WHERE p.type = (SELECT value FROM photo_type WHERE name = 'GALAXY')
  AND p.objid IS NOT NULL
photoobj_galaxy_cohort_48.description: Cohort view selecting photometric objects classified as galaxies. Exposes basic photometry and position for galaxy-level queries.

photoobj_with_type_name_49.name: photoobj_with_type_name_49
photoobj_with_type_name_49.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.type AS type,
  pt.value AS photo_type_value,
  pt.name AS photo_type_name,
  pt.description AS photo_type_description
FROM
  photoobj p
LEFT JOIN
  photo_type pt
ON
  p.type = pt.value
photoobj_with_type_name_49.description: Denormalized photoobj rows joined with photo_type lookup to expose human-readable type name and description alongside each photometric object.

photoobj_join_specobj.name: photoobj_join_specobj
photoobj_join_specobj.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.g AS g,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.bestobjid AS bestobjid,
  s.class AS class,
  s.z AS z
FROM photoobj_base p
JOIN specobj_base s
  ON p.objid = s.bestobjid
photoobj_join_specobj.description: Denormalized join of photoobj to specobj via photoobj.objid = specobj.bestobjid. Exposes photometric columns alongside spectroscopic class and redshift to support cohorts like 'spectroscopic galaxies with magnitude X'.

photo_with_spectro_match.name: photo_with_spectro_match
photo_with_spectro_match.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS objid,
  p.ra AS ra,
  p.dec AS dec,
  p.g AS g,
  s.specobjid AS specobjid,
  s.z AS spec_z,
  s.class AS spec_class,
  s.bestobjid AS bestobjid
FROM photoobj p
LEFT JOIN specobj s
  ON p.objid = s.bestobjid
photo_with_spectro_match.description: Denormalized join between photoobj and specobj on the canonical mapping (photoobj.objid = specobj.bestobjid), producing one row per photoobj with matching spectroscopic metadata when available.
